**F1 — NEAR AT FULL STRENGTH IS NOT 'Q152's six only' AT THE BASE'S SEED: the round's own new pin is red.** LINE 8 (6)
asks: the bands folder at the PR size, the base mirror first, then the tree at the base's printed seed — Q152's six red

Replayed alone in the clean mirror (`PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=1696442892 corepack pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=1
--silent=false packages/kernel/test/arr/bands/observer.test.ts -t 'arena form'`): the same failure, exit 1 —
deterministic at that seed. Twelve further PR-size runs of the test (`PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=1 … 12`): green. RELATED@1000
(seed 1790549561, 10 networks) and the builder's NEAR (seed −1088031545): green. So the pin is red at about one seed in
thirteen at the PR size: every later NEAR of the bands folder (round 2B's, the milestone's whole suite, each on a fresh
seed) can draw a red that is not Q152's.

*The cause, read in the code and replayed* (a mirror-only copy of the test printing both verdicts on the
counterexample; removed after): observer.test.ts:391-398 asserts that wherever the RECORD form (`judge`, samples every
GRID_CM = 20 cm) fails X + 10 cm, the ARENA form at the face's capped step (`judgeCapped`, step max(GRID_CM,
√(area ⁄ CAP_SAMPLES)) — 22.80 cm on this 2 080 000 cm² face) fails it too. That is not a property of the oracle. Both
forms skip every sample within MARGIN_CM of F's rings, of the truth's boundary and of X's own outline
(definition.ts:353-357 and :781-785), so a 10 cm translation leaves a detectable strip only 10 − 2 · MARGIN_CM ≈ 2 cm
wide; whether a sample falls in it is the grid's phase. On face 1 (left of the chord (121, 4000) → (919, 0), hw 10) the
20 cm grid has 13 samples in it (`(370, 2730) band read as kerb`, …; judged 4 873 of 5 200) and the 22.80 cm grid none
(judged 3 710 of 3 990, 0 misses: the strip shifts 4.55 cm a row against a 22.80 cm pitch — a near-exact period of five
rows that never meets the 2 cm window). The vertex check is step-independent but blind here: the two frame corners slide
along the horizontal frame sides, and the three band-side vertices of X + 10 land within MARGIN_CM of the chord's two
ends on the frame, where `bufferDepth` reads the pieces' seam (depth 0 – 2 cm, a lower bound: definition.ts:256-264) —
0 vertex faults in both forms. At step GRID_CM the arena form reads the record form's verdict figure for figure
(13 misses, judged 4 873 of 5 200): the two forms agree; the capped STEP is what loses the plant. No kernel code is
involved and X is right on this face (both forms clean unplanted).

*Why it fails the round and is not a note.* It is the line's own evidence, re-run as the line says, that differs (LINE
8: 'EACH ITEM FAILS THE ROUND where it differs'); NEAR is a gate, and a red outside the declared set in one of the
item's own test files is the item's (TEST SCOPE (2)); a pin that is red by the seed is the nondeterminism FAIL SAFE NOW
keeps in a round. It is test-side only and small.

*Required change (test-side only; no file under `packages/*/src`, no assertion of a test that existed before the round,
no existing export of definition.ts):* the arena-form pin of LINE 6 states only what holds at every seed. (i) THE TWO
FORMS AGREE AT ONE STEP: wherever the record form fails X + 10 cm, `judgeCapped(a.F, a.chains, X10, GRID_CM)` fails it
(this seat's replay: the same misses and judged counts); (ii) AT THE FACE'S CAPPED STEP the plant is asserted only where
the failure does not depend on the grid (the record form's verdict carries a vertex fault), and the sample-only cases
are COUNTED in the test's `OBSERVER arena form` line (caught k of n), never asserted; (iii) the counterexample is kept
as a named fixture (network `[{"a":11879,"b":919,"hw":10,"knots":null,"ends":"round"}]`, face 1: record 13 misses, arena
at its step 0 misses and 0 vertex faults, arena at GRID_CM 13); (iv) the test's title, the module comment's bullet
